key_insight: Stacking ensemble learning delivered the strongest predictive accuracy for UTS, weld hardness, and HAZ hardness, while multitask neural networks offered competitive shared-learning performance.
engineering_relevance: Accurate prediction of welding quality metrics can reduce trial-and-error in process optimization, helping engineers improve joint integrity and mechanical performance more efficiently.
method: Compared a multitask neural network (shared hidden layers with task-specific outputs) against stacking ensemble learning.
Used a shared welding dataset to predict UTS, weld hardness, and HAZ hardness simultaneously.
Evaluated both approaches with RMSE and R² across all three targets.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports RMSE and R² for each target, with stacking achieving lower errors and higher R² overall than the multitask neural network.
watch_item: Results are based on one shared dataset, so performance may change with different welding materials, process settings, or external validation data.
paper_title: A Comparative Analysis of Multitask Neural Networks and Stacking Ensemble Learning for Predicting UTS, Weld Hardness, and HAZ Hardness in Welding Applications
